content.text:
Worked example: A square has side 3 units. What is its area after the side is doubled?
1. New side = 3 × 2 = 6 units.
2. New area = 6 × 6 = 36 square units.
Answer: 36 square units

content.question: A square has side 3 units. What is its area after the side is doubled?

content.text:
A square's area is side times side.
Doubling the side multiplies the area by four.
content.publication_text:
A square's area is side times side.

content.text:
Figure it Out (2.1): A square has side 5 units. What is its area after the side is doubled?
1. New side = 5 × 2 = 10 units.
2. New area = 10 × 10 = 100 square units.
Answer: 100 square units

media.title: Double the Square

tool_config.title: Double the Square
tool_config.idea: Dragging the side of a square shows that doubling the side quadruples the area, not doubles it.
tool_config.screen: A square with a slider under it that sets the side length; the area is shown as a number next to the square.
student_does: Predict what happens to the area if the side doubles.
Drag the slider to double the side.
Read the new area off the square.
Compare the new area to the old area.
challenges: Set the side to 2 units; what is the area?
Set the side to 4 units; what is the area?
Set the side to 3 units; what is the area?
Set the side to 6 units; what is the area?
Double the side from 3 to 6 units; by what factor did the area grow?
feedback: A wrong guess still lets the slider move; the area number updates live either way.
A solved card shows the side and the area together, side by side with the previous card.
tool_config.done_when: The student has doubled a side at least once and named the area's growth factor out loud.

hint_ladder.text: What happens to area when a side is scaled?
Try doubling the side and read the new area.
Doubling the side gives 4 times the area, because area is side times side.

learning_objectives.objective_text: The student computes a square's area before doubling its side and again after doubling it, then compares the two areas to see the area grow by four times.
The student uses the tool to confirm that doubling a square's side multiplies its area by four, matching the worked computation done earlier in this topic.
